item.text: {"expression":"response_offset+drive_gain*u+wait_gain*h+memory_gain*memory","predicted_contrasts":["At fixed u and h, different histories predict different responses through memory; for positive tau, a newest isolated pulse has greater memory weight than an oldest isolated pulse.","For the same history and u, increasing h shifts the supplied negative times older relative to the response and reduces memory; the response change combines this with the explicit wait_gain*h term.","At fixed u and history, changing h tests whether the direct waiting-time effect and the wait-induced decay of memory are both needed."],"scientific_change":"Completes the history representation as a shared response law with an offset and separate drive, waiting-time, and memory coefficients. The large matched-u,h contrast between all-positive and all-negative histories motivates a history term; the contrast between equal-sum oldest and newest pulse histories motivates temporal weighting. The proposed paired pulse conditions vary pulse placement and waiting time to test those predictions. All four coefficients must be declared as shared response-unit parameters with finite bounds and initial values in a build step before fitting; they are not present in the fixed partial construction, so this expression is not currently fit-ready."}
